The ISO 28460 standard provides guidelines for the ship to shore LNG transfer at ports, compatibility, and safety measures between LNG carriers and terminal facilities. These marine standards could serve as a starting point for the development of aviation-specific standards that are in the early stages (ISO 2010). Determining the land requirements for an LNG storage farm sited in proximity to an airport is governed by several key factors, including storage capacity, equipment configuration, and mandated safety setbacks. Like hydrogen siting guidance, airport infrastructure, including ground support equipment, parked aircraft, and fuel storage tanks, is expected to be treated as a significant exposure concern with respect to siting LNG storage tanks. However, these aspects are not specifically discussed in the NFPA 59A (NFPA 2026b) code, which might need further review and safety analysis in terms of incorporating LNG infrastructure into airport environments. NFPA 59A (NFPA 2026b) recommends minimum separation distances for LNG storage tanks according to their storage capacities, which can vary for different configurations (i.e., single containment, double containment, or full containment tanks). For smaller capacities of cryogenic LNG storage tanks, which are often used for fueling vehicles or for small-scale distribution centers, separation distances from property lines and buildings can vary from a few meters up to tens of meters. With an increase in storage volume, setback distances also increase accordingly for better protection from thermal radiation and vapor dispersion hazards. To estimate the spatial footprint associated with LNG storage infrastructure, an example scenario with 4500 kg of LNG is considered here to match the same mass discussed previously for LH2. This storage capacity equates to a range bracket with 18,000-gallon as the maximum in Table 6.3.1 of NFPA 59 (NFPA 2026b), which corresponds to approximately 10.5 m³ of LNG using LNG density of approximately 430 kg/m³ (liquid density). Separation distances for LNG storage tanks are specified in NFPA 59A (NFPA 2026b). For LNG containers in this size range, the standard specifies a minimum setback distance of approximately 25 ft (7.6 m) from property lines and buildings that can be built upon. Assuming a representative vertical LNG tank diameter of approximately 2.4 m for a tank of this capacity, the total side length of the required safety zone can be estimated as the tank diameter plus twice the required setback distance (side length = tank diameter + 2 × setback distance) of 17.6 m (57.7 ft). Approximating the safety zone as a square area, the resulting spatial footprint is ~310 m² (3330 ft2). When normalized by the mass of LNG stored, this corresponds to a spatial footprint of approximately 0.069 m² per kilogram of LNG stored.
